hypocrisy

/hih-POK-ruh-see/ - the stress falls on POK · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Hypocrisy means professing standards that one's own conduct violates.

Diego spotted the hypocrisy at once: the pamphlet urging everyone to 'buy local' had been printed overseas to save its publisher a few dollars.

Example

The homeowners' association president campaigned on strict lawn rules and fined neighbors for stray dandelions, while behind her own tall fence the yard ran knee-deep in weeds. When a drone photo finally made the rounds, the uproar at the meeting was not about weeds at all—it was about the hypocrisy.

Hypocrisy needs both halves: the preaching and the violating. A messy yard alone is a lapse, and strict rules alone are zeal; professing the standard while secretly breaking it is what earns the sharper word.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

insincerity: Insincerity means saying what you do not mean — the compliment you do not feel, the promise you will not keep. Hypocrisy is a sharper, more specific failure: professing a standard while your own conduct violates it. A hypocrite may sincerely admire the standard; the offense is preaching it and breaking it.

phoniness: Phoniness is informal fakeness of any kind — a put-on accent, forced enthusiasm, a manufactured image — and it needs no moral rulebook at all. Hypocrisy is precisely moral: it requires a professed standard and conduct that violates it. Every hypocrite is phony about virtue; not every phony is a hypocrite.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

sincerity: meaning what you say

integrity: living by the values you claim, even when no one is watching

Where it sits · how much of the self is faked — inconsistency → hypocrisy → fraud

inconsistency vs. hypocrisy: Inconsistency just means words and actions drift apart now and then; hypocrisy is pointed—loudly professing the very standard you break.

fraud vs. hypocrisy: Fraud overshoots hypocrisy: the hypocrite fails to live up to real professed values, while the fraud's whole identity is a lie constructed for gain.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — hypo-

Prefix — hypo-: under

Root — crisy

Root — crisy: judging, deciding (from Greek krinein)

Put it together

Put it together: Hypo- (under) + crisy (judging, deciding) = deciding from under a mask. Greek hypokrisis meant play-acting—an actor 'answering from under' a stage mask—and hypokrites was simply the word for actor. The theater fell away and the mask stayed: a hypocrite performs virtue for the audience while living otherwise backstage.

Use the root in a new word: critic

Use the root in a new word: critic: A film critic spends her working life judging other people's movies.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral, morally charged

Hypocrisy names the gap itself between professed standards and actual conduct. Its partner in this unit, sanctimonious, describes the manner—the showy, lecturing display of virtue. A person can be quietly hypocritical with no sermon at all, and a sanctimonious lecture is hypocrisy only if the lecturer breaks the standard being preached.
